_strings.@@1ebf7ccac627: Retirement Income Credit — Taxpayer (and spouse, if filing jointly) who (a) has modified adjusted gross income less exemptions under $100,000; (b) received income from a pension, profit-sharing, or retirement plan (e.g., traditional IRA or 401(k)) on account of retirement; (c) the income is included in Ohio adjusted gross income; and (d) has not previously taken the Ohio lump sum retirement credit. Amounts deducted on the Ohio Schedule of Adjustments (e.g., Social Security, uniformed-services retirement) do not qualify.
_strings.@@2d4f415cbaf4: 2023 Ohio IT 1040 / SD 100 Instruction Booklet (Ohio Department of Taxation) — p. 46 table '2023 Ohio Income Tax Brackets for Ohio IT 1040' (0.000% to $26,050; $360.69 + 2.750% over $26,050; $2,394.32 + 3.688% over $100,000; $2,958.58 + 3.750% over $115,300); p. 17 'Line 8a – Tax on Line 7a' instruction and personal/dependent exemption table ($2,400/$2,150/$1,900 by MAGI); pp. 47-52 '2023 Income Tax Table for Ohio IT 1040'. Form line labels (lines 1-8c) and Schedule of Business Income lines 12-16 (3% business tax, $250,000/$125,000 business income deduction) verified from the 2023 IT 1040 form bundle at https://dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/tax.ohio.gov/forms/ohio_individual/individual/2023/1040-bundle-original.pdf

_strings.@@6a4b7b87005c: Ohio Earned Income Credit (EIC) — Resident/part-year/nonresident taxpayers who qualified for and claimed the federal Earned Income Tax Credit for tax year 2023 (federal Form 1040/1040-SR, line 27). Eligibility tracks the federal EIC.
_strings.@@763b3f95beb2: 2023 Ohio IT 1040 / SD 100 Instruction Booklet (Ohio Department of Taxation) - Line 1 federal AGI, Schedule of Adjustments additions/deductions, Who Must File, Ohio Residency, mailing addresses, due date, payment/check payee
_strings.@@88b8ba4a5d36: Treaty conformity — OH conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from OH income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the OH return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Ohio IT 1040 line 1 starts from federal adjusted gross income (federal 1040/1040-SR/1040-NR line 11) and the instructions state "Line 1 of your Ohio income tax return must match your federal adjusted gross income as defined in the Internal Revenue Code." Ohio AGI = line 1 + additions (Schedule of Adjustments) - deductions. The additions list (Sched. of Adjustments lines 8-11: 168(k)/179 depreciation add-backs, U.S. obligation interest/dividends exempt federally but not by the state, and federal conformity additions) contains NO add-back of federally treaty-exempt income. Therefore income excluded from federal AGI under a U.S. tax treaty flows through and is not re-taxed by Ohio. Federal-AGI common case, no treaty addback -> conforms.
_strings.@@ab357a529e3e: No separate nonresident/part-year return; nonresidents and part-year residents file the same Ohio IT 1040 and check the part-year resident or nonresident box. They compute the Nonresident Credit on form IT NRC (Ohio Nonresident Credit Calculation), which must be included with the IT 1040. (Optional residency status election: form IT NRS, Ohio Nonresident Statement.)

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: IT 1040 line 8a: "Nonbusiness income tax liability on line 7a (see instructions for tax tables)". Booklet p. 46 table headings: "Taxable Nonbusiness Income (Ohio IT 1040, line 7)" -> "Nonbusiness Income Tax (enter on Ohio IT 1040, line 8a)". Line 8c "Income tax liability before credits (line 8a plus line 8b)" adds the separate 3% business income tax (line 8b), which this op does not model. This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply 2023 Ohio IT 1040 line 7 (= line 7a), 'Taxable nonbusiness income (line 5 minus line 6; if negative, enter zero)'. Compute it on the form: line 3 Ohio adjusted gross income (federal AGI line 1 + Schedule of Adjustments additions line 2a - deductions line 2b), minus line 4 exemption amount (MAGI-tiered, see notes) = line 5 Ohio income tax base, minus line 6 taxable business income (Ohio Schedule of Business Income line 15) = line 7. This pack ships NO standard deduction and NO exemptions, so the engine applies the brackets directly to the figure you supply — do not pass federal AGI or Ohio AGI. CRITICAL — printed-constant divergence at $26,050: Ohio's published 2023 schedule (booklet p. 46) is discontinuous. It reads 0.000% up to $26,050, then '$360.69 plus 2.750% of the amount in excess of $26,050' — but the cumulative sum of the prior bracket is $0.00, not $360.69. Pure marginal bracket math cannot reproduce this fixed $360.69 jump, so this op's result is exactly $360.69 BELOW the form's printed schedule (and the booklet's tax table, which embeds it — e.g. the $26,050-$26,100 table band shows $361) for any line 7 amount over $26,050. The remaining printed constants ARE internally consistent with the marginal rates: $360.69 + 2.75% x $73,950 = $2,394.315 vs printed $2,394.32 (+$0.005), and $2,394.32 + 3.688% x $15,300 = $2,958.584 vs printed $2,958.58 (-$0.004). The filed form must use the printed brackets/table (R.C. 5747.02(A)(3)) — add $360.69 to this op's result when line 7 exceeds $26,050 to match the form. Tax table below $115,300: for line 7 amounts under $115,300, tax 'has been calculated for you' in the 2023 Income Tax Table (booklet pp. 47-52, $50-wide bands); p. 46 states taxpayers with taxable nonbusiness income of $115,300 or more MUST use the brackets. The line 8a instruction (p. 17) says 'All taxpayers can utilize the Income Tax Brackets' and warns 'The tax amount listed in the Income Tax Table may be slightly lower or higher than the tax amount computed by using the Income Tax Brackets' — table-band tax can differ by a few dollars within a band from exact bracket math. Personal/dependent exemption NOT shipped because it is income-dependent (booklet p. 17): $2,400 per exemption if modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) is $40,000 or less; $2,150 if MAGI is $40,001-$80,000; $1,900 if MAGI is more than $80,000. The same tiered amount applies to the taxpayer, spouse, and each dependent (IT 1040 line 4). MAGI = Ohio adjusted gross income (line 3) plus the business income deduction (Schedule of Adjustments line 12) (booklet p. 8, R.C. 5747.01(II)). A filer who can be claimed as a dependent on someone else's return gets $0 exemption for themselves. Compute line 4 on the form; supply line 7 to this op. Ohio has NO standard deduction and no itemized deduction; the only base reductions are the Schedule of Adjustments deductions (line 2b) and the line 4 exemption, both already reflected in the line 7 figure you supply. Business income is taxed SEPARATELY and is not modeled: taxable business income (IT 1040 line 6, after the business income deduction of $250,000 single/MFJ or $125,000 MFS) is taxed at a flat 3% on Ohio Schedule of Business Income line 16 and reported on IT 1040 line 8b; total income tax liability before credits is line 8c = 8a + 8b. The line 7 figure supplied to this op already excludes business income. One rate schedule for ALL filing statuses: Ohio's 2023 brackets do not vary by filing status (the p. 46 schedule prints a single set of brackets); the identical schedule is duplicated per status here. Qualifying surviving spouse shares the form's 'Single, head of household or qualifying surviving spouse' checkbox and maps to married_filing_jointly in the engine with an identical result. Ohio school district income tax (form SD 100) is a separate ADDITIONAL tax on top of the IT 1040 for residents of taxing school districts — not modeled by this op. Ohio's personal/dependent-linked 'exemption credit' is a CREDIT, not an exemption: $20 for each exemption claimed, on the Ohio Schedule of Credits line 9, only if MAGI less exemptions is under $30,000 (R.C. 5747.022) — it is subtracted from tax (IT 1040 line 9), never from income, and is not modeled. Other unmodeled credits include the joint filing credit (5-20% of tax, max $650), retirement income credit, senior citizen credit ($50), and Ohio EIC (30% of federal EIC). 2023 rate change: the booklet's 'Highlights for Tax Year 2023' (p. 5) states 'Ohio has reduced the number of tax brackets used to calculate tax on nonbusiness income and reduced two of the three tax rates.' The p. 46 schedule shipped here is the final published schedule the 2023 filing season used. Rounding: the form instructs 'Use whole dollars only' / 'Round all figures to the nearest dollar.'
